The decisive missing observation is the resolver's authorization and binding behavior: whether it checks the existing root against the caller's owner-aware view permission and returns HttpResponseForbidden when the caller lacks root access, and how it binds the requested version to the root and effective file. Thus the protected authorization object is the resolved root/document relationship, while the protected effect is serving the selected effective file for download; version ownership must not be substituted for root authorization. However, the supplied crop does not include the implementation of _resolve_request_and_root_doc or _get_effective_file_doc, so it does not source-prove that the resolver performs the accepted owner-aware view_document check on the root, nor exactly which concrete version/file object is selected. The source-visible result is therefore unknown rather than an inferred deny or allow. The decisive missing observation is the resolver's authorization and binding behavior: whether it checks the existing root against the caller's owner-aware view permission and returns HttpResponseForbidden when the caller lacks root access, and how it binds the requested version to the root and effective file. This addresses the entry, identity/resource binding, strongest visible control, protected effect, and missing-runtime/source fact questions without claiming repository-wide or deployment discovery.
